history.dynasty: None (modern temple; legend links it to the Mahabharata era)
history.summary: The Hanuman Mandir at Sector 8 (formerly Sihi village) is dedicated to Shri Ram and Hanuman and is built around a sacred pond where, per local legend retold in visitor accounts, Raja Janamejaya performed the Sarp Yajna to exterminate snakes, stopped at Rishi Astika's plea; serpent-king Vasuki is said to have blessed the pond's waters as curative, especially for skin ailments. The temple is spacious, stands near Surdaas Park and the Sant Surdas (Sihi) metro area, and is busiest on Tuesdays and Saturdays. IDENTITY NOTE: 'Hanuman Mandir, Faridabad' is a generic name with several prominent claimants, including Siddhpeeth Hanuman Mandir No. 2, K-Block (est. 28 Oct 1957, runs hanumanmandirfaridabad.org) and a Sector 6 shrine; the Sector 8/Sihi temple was chosen as the most prominent travel-listed referent, but this mapping should be reviewed. The Janamejaya legend is devotional lore from visitor reviews, not sourced history. Coordinates are a full-address geocode match.

name: Hanuman Mandir
town_description: Faridabad is the largest city in Haryana and part of the National Capital Region, an industrial hub founded in 1607 by Sufi saint Sheikh Farid (Baba Farid). It lies about 25 km south of Delhi on NH-19 (Mathura Road).

travel.railway: Faridabad New Town railway station (~2 km)
travel.road: Near Surdaas Park on the Sector 7-8 dividing road; Escorts Mujesar metro station nearby; autos and e-rickshaws available

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; early mornings, or Tuesdays/Saturdays (expect crowds)
